subject: Commit acceleration: renewal playbook & QBR scheduling
messages:
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightpath.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit acceleration: renewal playbook & QBR scheduling

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off a short renewal-orchestration plan so we can lock in the uplift and capacity increase without disrupting your production windows. High level:

- Target go-forward: annual renewal with a 25% committed token uplift + 2 reserved GPU slots for peak batch jobs.
- Timeline: finalize commercial terms and SOW by Nov 20; QBR + ops review week of Nov 30; production uplift targeting Dec 15.
- Critical stakeholders: Alex (product owner), Procurement, CS (Marissa), Solutions (Karthik), and Redwood sales (me).

Attached is a draft renewal playbook with an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and dependencies flagged. I’ve also dropped a Calendly link below to book a 45‑minute QBR/technical sync — please pick two options so we have fallback windows.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alex: confirm committed token uplift percentage and any procurement timing constraints by Nov 6.
2) Procurement: share PO/standard terms window and preferred billing cadence.
3) Marissa & Karthik: prep a short ops runbook and capacity plan for the QBR.

Attachments: renewal_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook), MAP_draft.xlsx (mutual action plan - draft)

Calendly: https://calendly.com/soojin-lee/brightpath-qbr

Appreciate a quick ack so I can lock the QBR slots.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alex Wu <alex@brightpath.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightpath.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit acceleration: renewal playbook & QBR scheduling

Soojin —

Thanks, this is very helpful. Quick answers:
- The product team is aligned on the 25% uplift but we need clarity on burst capacity for batch jobs during end-of-month processing. Can Marissa/Karthik include a worst-case throughput plan?
- Procurement: we typically need a two-week review window for any contract amendments. PO issuance target is Nov 16 if terms are final by Nov 10.

I booked two times on the Calendly — Nov 30 at 11:00am PT and Dec 1 at 9:00am PT as backups.

One ask from my side: can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee a maximum token latency at the committed burst SLA, or whether we should plan for the fallback routing policy described in the playbook? That will affect how we size reserved slots.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Wu
Head of Product, BrightPath AI
alex@brightpath.ai | +1 617-555-0188

Cc: Alex Wu <alex@brightpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit acceleration: renewal playbook & QBR scheduling

Looping in a short ops checklist and a throughput sketch — see inline. We should reserve up to 3 GPUs for the first month of uplift as a conservative buffer; we can scale that down after we observe the first two weekly batch runs. Karthik, can you add expected 95th/99th percentile token latency numbers for the proposed reserved slots? If we can commit to latency SLOs by broad class (interactive vs batch), Alex can decide on fallback routing policies.

Inline notes: 
- MAP: add "procurement sign-off" row with target Nov 16.
- QBR agenda: 1) Business goals & KPI mapping (10m) 2) Capacity plan & SLOs (15m) 3) Migration / uplift runbook (10m) 4) Commercial sign-off & next steps (10m)

I attached a quick runbook template (copied below) and a one-pager ops FAQ — happy to iterate tonight if needed.

Attachments referenced: MAP_draft.xlsx (updated by me after the QBR)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 212-555-0123

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit acceleration: renewal playbook & QBR scheduling

Alex / team —

Great — thanks for booking the times. I’ve locked the Nov 30, 11:00am PT slot as primary and left Dec 1 as the fallback. Calendar invites sent.

Quick answers to Alex’s question: Marissa & Karthik will bring an initial SLO matrix and a conservative reserve plan (3 GPUs) to the QBR; we will include fallback routing as an explicit play in the MAP so you have deterministic behavior if capacity gets constrained. If procurement can aim to surface redlines by Nov 10, legal can triage quickly and we can hit the Nov 16 PO target.

Attached final: renewal_playbook_v1.pdf (updated with fallback routing appendix) and MAP_draft.xlsx (updated with procurement row). I’ll also open a HubSpot task for procurement follow-up and add the DocuSign link when we have final terms.

DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/some-ds-link
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Thanks everyone — see you at the QBR.

—Soojin
